For commercial re-use, please contact journals.permissions@oup.com Abstract Objective To examine disease and target engagement biomarkers in the RISE-SSc trial of riociguat in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis and their potential to predict the response to treatment. Methods Patients were randomized to riociguat ( n = 60) or placebo ( n = 61) for 52 weeks. Skin biopsies and plasma/serum samples were obtained at baseline and week 14. Plasma cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) was assessed using radio-immunoassay. α-Smooth muscle actin (αSMA) and skin thickness were determined by immunohistochemistry, mRNA markers of fibrosis by qRT-PCR in skin biopsies, and serum CXC motif chemokine ligand 4 (CXCL-4) and soluble platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule-1 (sPECAM-1) by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Results By week 14, cGMP increased by 94 (78)% with riociguat and 10 (39)% with placebo ( P < 0.001, riociguat vs placebo). Serum sPECAM-1 and CXCL-4 decreased with riociguat vs placebo ( P = 0.004 and P = 0.008, respectively). There were no differences in skin collagen markers between the two groups. Higher baseline serum sPECAM-1 or the detection of αSMA-positive cells in baseline skin biopsies was associated with a larger reduction of modified Rodnan skin score from baseline at week 52 with riociguat vs placebo (interaction P -values 0.004 and 0.02, respectively). Conclusion Plasma cGMP increased with riociguat, suggesting engagement with the nitric oxide–soluble guanylate cyclase–cGMP pathway. Riociguat was associated with a significant reduction in sPECAM-1 (an angiogenic biomarker) vs placebo. Elevated sPECAM-1 and the presence of αSMA-positive skin cells may help to identify patients who could benefit from riociguat in terms of skin fibrosis. Introduction Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a severe and debilitating autoimmune connective tissue disease. It is characterized by fibrosis, inflammation, microvascular injury and systemic organ manifestations including pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), interstitial lung disease, renal dysfunction and failure, diffuse gastrointestinal disease, and myocardial involvement [ 1–4 ]. The nitric oxide (NO)–soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC)–cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) pathway plays an important role in tissue homeostasis through various mechanisms including antifibrotic and anti-inflammatory effects [ 5 , 6 ]. In preclinical in vitro and in vivo studies, the soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator riociguat exhibited anti-inflammatory, antifibrotic and antiproliferative effects mediated partly by the attenuation of TGF-β signalling [ 5–7 ]. The phase 3 PATENT trial of riociguat in PAH [ 8 , 9 ] included a subgroup with PAH associated with SSc, in whom riociguat prevented the decline in functional capacity and was well tolerated [ 10 ]. In addition, riociguat improved digital blood flow in some patients with Raynaud’s phenomenon in a single-dose pilot study [ 11 ]. These observations suggested that riociguat may reduce tissue fibrosis in SSc, and led to the investigation of riociguat in the phase 2b RIociguat Safety and Efficacy in patients with early diffuse cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis (RISE-SSc) study [ 12 ]. Treatment with riociguat for 52 weeks did not significantly improve the primary end point (modified Rodnan skin score [mRSS]) vs placebo; however, a numerical decrease in mRSS was seen with riociguat ( P = 0.08 vs placebo) and analyses of secondary and exploratory endpoints showed potential efficacy [ 12 ]. Prognostic biomarkers help to identify patients who are at high risk for certain disease outcomes, such as organ involvement or death in patients with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc), irrespective of treatment. Predictive biomarkers allow physicians to predict response to treatment [ 13 ]. Both types of biomarkers may help to inform clinical decision-making and efforts have been made to identify predictive parameters for disease progression in dcSSc [ 14–16 ]. Target engagement biomarkers confirm delivery of the drug and indicate that it is acting on its target. This report describes the pre-specified exploratory biomarker analysis from RISE-SSc. The objectives were to examine the effects of riociguat on its target pharmacological pathway, to investigate the prognostic value of biomarkers in the placebo group (who did not receive targeted treatments for SSc other than rescue therapy at investigator discretion from week 26), and to investigate whether biomarkers could predict the effects of riociguat on skin fibrosis, measures of disease activity and progression of lung disease.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated disease and target engagement biomarkers in the phase 2b RISE-SSc trial of riociguat in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc) to predict treatment response. While the primary endpoint (modified Rodnan Skin Score, mRSS) did not reach statistical significance, riociguat treatment significantly increased plasma cGMP levels, indicating engagement of the NO-sGC-cGMP pathway. Additionally, serum sPECAM-1 and CXCL-4 levels decreased with riociguat. Elevated baseline sPECAM-1 and the presence of αSMA-positive cells in skin biopsies were identified as potential predictive biomarkers for greater mRSS reduction with riociguat, suggesting these markers may help identify patients who could benefit from the treatment for skin fibrosis.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patients with early treatment-naïve diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis were randomized to receive riociguat (n=60) or placebo (n=61) for 52 weeks. Riociguat was administered up to 2.5 mg, maximum three times daily. Biomarker assessments were performed at baseline (day 0) and week 14, with clinical endpoints evaluated up to week 52. Rescue therapy was permitted from week 26. While cGMP changes correlated with riociguat pharmacokinetics, no explicit dose-response comparisons for other biomarkers were formally reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased by 94 (78)% (from 7.22 ± 2.57 to 12.92 ± 5.24 pmol/ml) with riociguat vs. 10 (39)% (from 7.44 ± 3.34 to 7.50 ± 3.02 pmol/ml) with placebo by week 14 (P < 0.001). Elevated levels correlated with riociguat pharmacokinetic variables, but showed no clear relationship with mRSS change in the riociguat group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Marker of activation of the nitric oxide–soluble guanylate cyclase–cGMP pathway, playing an important role in tissue homeostasis through antifibrotic, anti-inflammatory, and vasodilatory effects.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Riociguat treatment in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (RISE-SSc trial) from baseline to week 14.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates pharmacodynamic engagement of riociguat with the NO-sGC-cGMP pathway, suggesting potential improvement in vascular function and antifibrotic/anti-inflammatory effects. No clear predictive value for mRSS response.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: sPECAM-1 (soluble platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule-1)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased with riociguat vs placebo by week 14 (mean change –11.91% vs 2.18%, P = 0.004). Higher baseline serum sPECAM-1 was associated with greater mRSS reduction at week 52 with riociguat (interaction P = 0.004), while in the placebo group, higher baseline levels correlated with mRSS increase.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An angiogenic and inflammatory marker, involved in leukocyte transmigration and endothelial protection.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Baseline levels and riociguat treatment in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (RISE-SSc trial).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated baseline sPECAM-1 predicts a greater reduction in mRSS with riociguat treatment, while in placebo patients, it indicates progression of skin fibrosis. A decrease with riociguat suggests anti-inflammatory and angiogenic effects and potential for greater treatment response.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased with riociguat vs placebo by week 14 (mean change –13.56% vs 5.74%, P = 0.008). Baseline levels showed a correlation of 0.377 with change in mRSS in the riociguat group but no clear predictive value for mRSS at week 52 (interaction P > 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An inflammatory marker that mediates fibrosis by promoting myofibroblast transformation and collagen production; released upon platelet activation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Riociguat treatment in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (RISE-SSc trial) from baseline to week 14.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Elevated in SSc and correlates with lung fibrosis and PAH. Reduction by riociguat suggests anti-inflammatory properties and potential benefit for peripheral vasculopathy, though no clear predictive value for overall mRSS response was established.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: associated with greater mRSS reduction with riociguat; associated with less mRSS improvement in placebo
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Detection of αSMA-positive cells in baseline skin biopsies was associated with a larger reduction of modified Rodnan skin score from baseline at week 52 with riociguat vs placebo (interaction P=0.02). In the placebo arm, αSMA-positive patients showed less improvement in mRSS, with 40% experiencing mRSS progression, compared to 8% in the riociguat arm. No direct effect of riociguat on αSMA staining was observed.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Marker of myofibroblast activation and extracellular matrix production, key in fibrotic processes.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Baseline αSMA status and riociguat treatment in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (RISE-SSc trial).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: The presence of αSMA-positive skin cells at baseline indicates myofibroblast activation and predicts a greater therapeutic response to riociguat in terms of skin fibrosis reduction, especially in patients with specific autoantibodies and higher baseline mRSS. In placebo-treated patients, αSMA positivity predicted less mRSS improvement and higher progression.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The primary endpoint, change in mRSS from baseline to week 52, did not significantly improve with riociguat vs placebo (P = 0.08). Mean mRSS was 16.8 (±3.7) at baseline, changing to 14.6 (±6.6) in the riociguat group and 15.7 (±10.5) in the placebo group at week 52.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Clinical indicator of skin thickness, fibrosis, and overall disease severity in systemic sclerosis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Riociguat treatment in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (RISE-SSc trial) from baseline to week 52.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects skin fibrosis and disease progression. While not statistically significant for the primary endpoint, a numerical decrease was observed with riociguat.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences in mean fold-changes from baseline to week 14 between riociguat and placebo groups for Collagen 1A1 (riociguat: 1.27, placebo: 0.96), Collagen 1A2 (riociguat: 1.24, placebo: 1.11), or Collagen 3A1 (riociguat: 1.21, placebo: 1.05). Collagen 1A1 mRNA fold-change showed a modest correlation (0.339) with mRSS change in the riociguat group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Components of the extracellular matrix, reflecting fibrotic gene expression and structural integrity of the skin.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Riociguat treatment in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (RISE-SSc trial) from baseline to week 14.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: No significant change suggests riociguat did not reverse advanced fibrosis at the mRNA level. Modest correlation for Collagen 1A1 mRNA with mRSS changes may indicate some association with skin fibrosis progression.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences in changes from baseline to week 14 between riociguat and placebo groups.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Endogenous inhibitor of nitric oxide synthase, impacting NO bioavailability and vascular function.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Riociguat treatment in dcSSc patients from baseline to week 14.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Levels are elevated in diffuse SSc, but no change was observed with riociguat treatment, suggesting no direct impact on its levels or the overall NO-sGC-cGMP pathway engagement via ADMA.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences in changes from baseline to week 14 between riociguat and placebo groups.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Related to NO metabolism; an indicator of renal function and cardiovascular risk.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant differences in changes from baseline to week 14 between riociguat and placebo groups (assessed by immunohistochemistry).
